This means that although I know all phenomena in every aspect through the wisdom of omniscience, which is gathered by conventional cognition, when categorized by ultimate wisdom, it is as if one sees objects in a dream. It is the expression meaning that not even one phenomenon to be known is seen. O sons of the gods, because all phenomena are completely pure, this refers to the non-existence of things being called purity. It is the expression meaning that they are entirely non-existent. O Blessed One, awakening to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is not difficult. This is because all phenomena are non-existent; it is not difficult to realize that which is non-existent as being non-existent. It is difficult to realize the true nature of existing phenomena exactly as they are. To know and practice the non-existence of things that do not exist is not difficult. In this way, if phenomena existed, one would have to practice the conduct of the perfections and so forth, in order to increase virtuous qualities and abandon non-virtuous ones. Since these phenomena do not exist, the practice is not difficult. Therefore, it is said that attaining full awakening is not difficult. The intention of the Venerable Sariputra, who stated that full awakening is difficult, is as follows: having understood that all phenomena are by nature non-existent, like the sky, if it were sufficient to simply remain silent, then it would not be difficult. However, in reality, one must both understand that there is no awakening to all phenomena, and subsequently engage in the practices of the perfections, while also fully understanding all phenomena.

The complexion of the Thus-Gone One's natural body is unlike that of humans or gods, and there is nothing in the world that resembles it. Although it appears to have a complexion, all who see it know that it is not like the complexion of our own bodies. Likewise, while it possesses flesh, bones, hair, and nails, it is not like that of any other sentient being. Even though it appears as such, it arouses wonder in all worldly beings.

Thus, the body exists as the essence of a body, yet it appears in that manner. Although worldly beings are moved to wonder, no one can comprehend what its nature truly is. In this way, even though it resembles the bodies of all others in shape, form, and so forth, its true nature is unknown. Due to the intermediate eon of famine, the unbearable suffering of famine arises in the world from time to time. Due to the intermediate eon of disease, many illnesses arise. Due to the intermediate eon of weapons, there arises much mutual harm of one against another. 

Due to the power of destruction by water, the aspect of emotional affliction <term>klesha</term> <gloss>defilement or disturbing emotion</gloss> becomes predominant; due to the power of destruction by fire, the aspect of hatred becomes predominant; and due to the power of destruction by wind, the aspect of ignorance becomes predominant. The corruption of lifespan is such that there is no certainty regarding the life of sentient beings. At times, the lifespan is immeasurable. At other times, it diminishes to ten years. Even that is uncertain. Some die while in the womb. Others die immediately upon birth, in childhood, in youth, in adulthood, at the peak of maturity, in middle age, or in old age. Because there is no certainty, there exists in the world much sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and mental distress.

The corruption of views consists of extremely bad views that destroy all virtue, which, when analyzed distinctly, total sixty-two. Those who are firmly committed to such wrong views cannot be healed even by a thousand Buddhas. Moreover, all non-Buddhist sectarians are of a nature that disparages <note>the teachings</note>, lack faith, do not gather <note>in virtuous assemblies</note>, are highly despicable, and are not vessels by nature. Homage to Manjushri, the Youthful.

Why was this sutra, titled "The Great Bodhisattva Should Not Abandon These Four Dharmas Even for the Sake of Their Own Life Until They Die," composed? It is to correctly instruct those who are confused about the methods for attaining supreme enlightenment while having entered the Great Vehicle; to correctly uphold those who are heedless; to correctly uplift those who are habitually discouraged; and to make those who have correctly entered the path rejoice.

The number four is stated to avoid confusion from excessive length and to prevent those who do not wish to listen from abandoning the teaching. When a number is stated, it is for the sake of easy recollection. Regarding the patience and gentleness that appear later, they are not separate because they share a single purpose.

Although there are many synonyms for those who have entered the Great Vehicle, two names are mentioned due to three causes: aspiration, application, and realization. What is meant by aspiration? They are called <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>enlightenment-being</gloss> because they aspire to profound objects of knowledge. They are called <term>Mahasattva</term> <gloss>great being</gloss> because they aspire to great power.

What is meant by application? It is for the sake of exerting oneself for supreme, perfectly completed enlightenment, and for the sake of fully protecting all sentient beings from suffering.

<margin>What it is to correct medically.</margin>
*To correct is to take the corrected.* Whoever is malicious and has sinned, if he is punished, the correction does not extend further than the will of him who has been punished endures. Such are these corrections as well; it is placed with them, not with you. Now, in this case, the physician has nothing more to consider than that the poison be taken away. That must be done through separation. As, for example: a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted into food. If you take the poison away from it, you may eat it without harm. The same is to be understood equally concerning all other things, namely, that the work requires a similar separation. That not yet being done, you cannot be secure in your operation; unless perhaps it happens that nature supplies your shortcomings, or a greater kindness of heaven favors you. For in your art, there will be no help left over.

Now, therefore, if that true foundation is indeed necessary which removes the poison, how does Alchemy achieve this? For it must necessarily be done in such a way that, if Mars <note>alchemical term for iron</note> is in the Sun <note>alchemical term for gold</note>, the Mars is removed, and if Saturn <note>alchemical term for lead</note> is found in Venus <note>alchemical term for copper</note>, it is separated from it. For as many ascendants and impressions as there are in the things of nature, so many bodies also exist in them. But those bodies which are contrary, it is necessary that some of them be entirely taken away and removed, so that in this way all contrariety is lifted, and the evil which you seek is removed from the good.
<margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin>
Just as gold is useful for nothing unless it is first cast into the fire, so much less useful is a medicine which does not pass through the fire. For it is necessary that all things pass through fire into another generation, which ought to benefit and aid man. And should this not rightfully be considered the proper foundation of any physician? For the physician ought not to apply poisons, but true arcana.
